answer: A wildfire-response market pays agents for alerts only when a calibrated camera at an ocean-facing canyon records an ember and an independently operated thermal sensor confirms the same event within a short window. One event ID earns one fixed fee, regardless of how many accounts relay it. To multiply fees, an attacker must deploy distinct calibrated devices and risk a bond on false reports; aliases alone gain nothing. Coordinated sensor owners could still fabricate readings, so surprise field checks and public challenges remain necessary.
